Model.description: Render a triangle mesh as a scene entity. Supply a WebGPUMesh, CPU vertex arrays, or existing GPU buffers, then choose shading and texture maps independently of the geometry. Model combines ModelGeometry, ModelFragment and ModelRenderer components.

Box.description: Create a rectangular 3D mesh with independently specified width, height and depth. Its inherited Model methods provide material styling, mesh updates and scene transforms.

Sprite.description: Display an image, video, canvas, render texture or atlas region on a rectangular quad. A SubTexture selects shared image coordinates; updateSize changes the quad while setSource changes its content.

Mask.description: Clip content to a VectorEntity boundary, or invert the boundary to reveal content outside it. The mask owns its shape and content as children and patches their stencil behavior. Move the content when you want the picture to travel inside a stationary boundary.

FontLoader.description: Load vector fonts or MSDF fonts through one asynchronous entry point. Font sources can be local files, URLs, Google Font names or pre-baked descriptors. Its caches avoid repeating atlas generation, and persistence is an explicit option.

FunctionGraph2D.description: Sample a scalar function on a CoordinateSystem and render its curve, with optional area fill. A tracker or other changing input must be followed by graph resampling to update existing geometry.

Animator.description: Build target-state changes for an entity animation.
notes: Builder methods do not generally apply the final target immediately. Scene.play prepares and schedules the returned animation.
Pivot setup can synchronize offsets on the live entity to keep the visible position stable, so target construction is not entirely free of side effects.

Code.description: Present syntax-highlighted source as scene content. This is a renderable code display with line and token geometry, rather than the documentation site’s editable TypeScript viewer.

GradientFill.description: Describe a gradient fill through colors and gradient parameters. Assign the effect through the material/shader styling path to change the appearance of a vector interior.

SubScene.description: Attach a nested Scene as an Entity in another scene graph. Its update method links the nested scene to its parent’s composer resources and forwards time updates. The constructor calls the nested scene’s init and run before this resource linking, so setup that requires a device needs care.

ZoomView.description: Show a magnified copy of an entity inside a display window while marking the corresponding focus region. Change the focus position or zoom factor to guide attention to a detail; its borders and background can be styled separately.

RenderConfig.description: Collect renderer choices for antialiasing, transparency, shadows, culling, shading and path tracing. Its defaults describe the starting configuration; enabling an effect also depends on the active rendering pipeline and supported resources.

VertexSchema.description: Generate matching WGSL input declarations and GPUVertexBufferLayout data from named attribute types. Attribute order controls offsets and shader locations. Use instance step mode for data that advances per instance instead of per vertex.

GPUAllocator.description: Allocate buffers with a nonzero size and four-byte alignment. Its safeCreateBuffer helper guards empty or invalid size calculations before handing the descriptor to WebGPU.

ComputeBufferPool.description: Reuse transient GPU buffers by usage and rounded size within the frame lifecycle. Buffers are returned to the pool on resetForNewFrame; data that must survive across frames needs separately owned storage.

SDFText.description: Render typography using signed-distance glyph textures. Font metrics determine layout and bounds, while the text entity still participates in the normal scene graph, styling and animation system.

SDFEntity3D.description: Render a spatial signed distance field as an entity. Compose the field first, then use the entity’s material, transform and camera framing to inspect the volume.

PathGeometry.description: Store and process vector path geometry for the path rendering pipeline. Path is the author-facing entity; this component manages the geometric data it submits to rendering.

LineGeometry.description: Store line geometry and its GPU data as a component. It supports the line entity’s rendering path while the entity owns placement and style.

ModelGeometry.description: Manage a model’s mesh data and GPU buffers. Use Model for ordinary scene authoring; inspect this component when implementing mesh updates or integrating an existing buffer.

TextGeometry.description: Provide glyph geometry for text entities. It connects typography layout with the component rendering path.

SVG.description: Load and represent SVG artwork as a scene-graph hierarchy. Parsed shapes retain their own paths and styling, so an SVG can be transformed as a whole or inspected through its children.

SVGPath.description: Represent an SVG path within the imported artwork hierarchy. The path data describes geometry, while inherited vector styling and transforms control its scene appearance.

SolidFill.description: Supply a uniform fill effect for the vector material pipeline. It provides a simple alternative to a gradient or procedural interior.

Line.description: Build a polyline from points and style its outline. Use setVertices to replace its points after input or data changes; its transform can move the entire line without rewriting those points.

Line3D.description: Build a line in spatial coordinates using the 3D line rendering path. It is useful for axes, edges and curves that must participate in a spatial scene.

PolarCurve.description: Render a curve described in polar coordinates against a coordinate system. The mathematical input describes radius as angle changes; the plotting entity maps the samples into the scene.

Mat4.description: Store and compute four-by-four matrices used for spatial transforms and projection. Check each method’s signature and implementation when deciding whether to reuse a matrix or copy it before mutation.

Mat3.description: Store and compute three-by-three matrices for linear algebra and transformation helpers. Reuse matrix instances in repeated calculations when the chosen operation permits it.

FadeIn.description: Animate an entity from an invisible appearance toward its visible state. Place the object before playback so the fade communicates arrival without mixing in an unintended position change.

Create.description: Reveal an existing entity through its creation animation. An entity can provide createAnim for custom choreography; composite creation can distribute work across children.

CameraDollyZoom.description: Combine camera translation with field-of-view changes to alter perspective while controlling the subject’s framing. The camera animation uses a target reference to determine the relationship between those changes.

OfflineRecorder.description: Record rendered frames for an offline export. This belongs to the export pipeline; live documentation playback is a browser scene preview rather than a completed recording.

OfflineRenderManager.description: Coordinate offline rendering for a composer, including output timing and recorder state. Use the export workflow when frame consistency and a finished media artifact matter.

RealTime.description: Track elapsed real time and delta time for playback. Pausing and resuming must account for the gap so a stopped scene does not jump by the wall-clock duration on resume.

PlayerControls.description: Provide the engine’s timeline playback controls. These operate on scene playback; an application’s external timers and DOM handlers need their own lifecycle management.

PostProcessPass.description: Apply a post-processing stage to rendered output. It belongs after scene rendering, so the effect changes the image rather than the original entity geometry.

RenderPass.description: Represent a renderer pass with its attachments and drawing behavior. Inspect pass configuration when extending the rendering pipeline or diagnosing ordering and depth/stencil behavior.

Pass.description: Represent a unit of work in the frame graph. Declared resources and dependencies let the graph schedule work and manage intermediate allocations.

ResourcePool.description: Reuse intermediate resources for the frame graph. Resource lifetime and compatibility determine which allocations can be shared safely.

PersistentRenderTexture.description: Keep a render texture across frames for effects that depend on prior output. Explicitly manage its updates and cleanup because persistence changes the resource’s lifetime.

GeometryComponent.description: Base component contract for entity geometry. A geometry component prepares geometric data while renderer and fragment components handle how that data becomes pixels.

AreaChart.description: Plot a filled Cartesian data series using the chart library. Axes and series configuration turn data coordinates into a visual area; use it when the magnitude and shape of the region are part of the comparison.

Graph.description: Represent and display graph nodes and edges through the graph library. Layout choices determine where nodes sit, while edge styling and transitions explain relationships.

Automaton.description: Represent an automaton through states, transitions and input-driven traversal. It supplies the graph structure used by the automata examples to make state changes visible.

Layouts.description: Provide graph layout strategies that assign node positions. Choose a layout that makes the graph’s structure readable before adding transitions or traversal highlights.

Rapier2DBackend.description: Implement the 2D physics backend contract with Rapier. The physics plugin connects its bodies and world stepping to scene entities.

Rapier3DBackend.description: Implement the 3D physics backend contract with Rapier. Use the physics plugin to manage world initialization and synchronize simulated bodies with scene transforms.

PhysicsUtils.description: Provide mesh and shape conversion helpers for the 3D physics integration. These bridge renderable geometry and the data needed by physics collision shapes.
